editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, with no drift or hallucination. The pre-flight checks, the use cases, the TEM-vs-PEC shot claim and the circuit/application function split all match the English, and the "tu" register holds. A native editor would still fix a few calques and stiff phrases. Entry [63] reads "performance de qualité utilitaire dès la sortie de la boîte" and renders "pattern" as "modèle", which clashes with "modèles" (templates) in [30]/[31]. Entry [30] renders "swap in" as "échanger", and [16] has the awkward "n'effectue pas l'exécution".

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box ... rather than building the pattern for each problem from scratch
examples.translation: pour rendre accessible une performance de qualité utilitaire dès la sortie de la boîte ... plutôt que de construire le modèle pour chaque problème à partir de zéro
examples.suggested: pour offrir d'emblée des performances à l'échelle utilitaire ... plutôt que de construire le pattern Qiskit de chaque problème à partir de zéro
examples.why: "dès la sortie de la boîte" is a literal calque of "out of the box". Rendering "pattern" (a Qiskit pattern) as "modèle" makes it look like the "modèles" (templates) the same page talks about.

examples.source: allows you to swap in new tools, methods, or configurations
examples.translation: te permet d'échanger de nouveaux outils, méthodes ou configurations
examples.suggested: te permet d'intégrer facilement de nouveaux outils, méthodes ou configurations
examples.why: "échanger" reads as trading things away. The source means plugging in or substituting new components.

examples.source: and skip the run if there is not enough left to finish it
examples.translation: et n'effectue pas l'exécution s'il n'en reste pas assez pour la terminer
examples.suggested: et renonce à l'exécution s'il n'en reste pas assez pour la mener à bien
examples.why: This phrasing is stiff and reads like machine translation.

examples.source: with which users can scale successfully to larger problems
examples.translation: avec lesquelles les utilisateurs peuvent passer à l'échelle avec succès pour des problèmes plus grands
examples.suggested: qui permettent aux utilisateurs de passer avec succès à des problèmes de plus grande taille
examples.why: The relative clause copies the English structure and reads clumsily.

editor_note: Nothing in the file would mislead a learner. Dates, figures and caveats all carry over correctly: the rep_delay ranges, "au plus tôt le 30 septembre", the retirement windows and the limits of the exploratory QPU. The problems are consistency ones. "job" is kept as "job" in the recent entries but becomes "tâche(s)" in the older ones ([149], [176], [187], [195], [239], [256]). "gate" is kept as "gates" ([17], [86], [122], [258]) but becomes "portes" in [272], [277] and [280]. The formal "Notez que" appears in the middle of otherwise "tu" prose ([61], [88], [110], [119], [160], [233]). Smaller points: "1 juillet"/"1 novembre" should be "1er", and UI labels switch between English and French ("Compute resources" vs "Ressources de calcul", "Instance access" vs "Accès à l'instance").

examples.source: *Note that before submitting jobs, you should verify compatibility...
examples.translation: *Notez qu'avant de soumettre des jobs, tu dois vérifier la compatibilité...
examples.suggested: *Note qu'avant de soumettre des jobs, tu dois vérifier la compatibilité...
examples.why: This mixes vous and tu inside one sentence. The same formal "Notez" also appears in [88], [110], [119], [160] and [233].

examples.source: Once this QPU is retired, it will no longer accept jobs. If any jobs are queued...
examples.translation: Une fois ce QPU retiré, il n'acceptera plus de tâches. Si des tâches sont en file d'attente...
examples.suggested: Une fois ce QPU retiré, il n'acceptera plus de jobs. Si des jobs sont en file d'attente...
examples.why: Most of the file keeps "job" (e.g. [93], [98], [107]), so switching to "tâches" in the older entries is inconsistent.

examples.source: not compatible with fractional gates, pulse gates, or dynamic circuits
examples.translation: n'est pas compatible avec les portes fractionnaires, les portes d'impulsion ou les circuits dynamiques
examples.suggested: n'est pas compatible avec les gates fractionnaires, les gates d'impulsion ou les circuits dynamiques
examples.why: [258] renders the same concept as "gates fractionnaires" just above, so the gate term is split between "gates" and "portes" within the file.

examples.source: it will no longer be accessible starting 1 July 2025
examples.translation: elle ne sera plus accessible à partir du 1 juillet 2025
examples.suggested: elle ne sera plus accessible à partir du 1er juillet 2025
examples.why: French writes the first day of the month as "1er". The same slip is in [175], [221] and [233].

examples.source: a new Instance access section shows all instances that grant you access
examples.translation: une nouvelle section Accès à l'instance affiche toutes les instances
examples.suggested: une nouvelle section Instance access affiche toutes les instances
examples.why: [116] keeps the UI label "Instance access" in English, and [113] vs [143] likewise split "Compute resources" and "Ressources de calcul". UI labels should be rendered one way throughout.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner: the beta caveat and the version requirement (0.47.0 ou supérieure) in [11] and the resilience_level wording in [7] are all kept. In [6], the gloss 'extinction d'erreur de lecture par embrouillage (TREX)' translates 'twirling' as 'embrouillage' (scrambling), which is imprecise. French quantum writers usually keep the English name 'Twirled Readout Error eXtinction' or write 'twirling'. There is also a small calque: 'démontre comment' should be 'montre comment'.

examples.source: Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX)
examples.translation: l'extinction d'erreur de lecture par embrouillage (TREX)
examples.suggested: Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX), l'extinction d'erreur de lecture par twirling
examples.why: Twirling is Pauli randomization, not scrambling. 'embrouillage' is not the conventional term, and the proper-noun method name is usually kept in English.

examples.source: demonstrates how this model is used
examples.translation: démontre comment ce modèle est utilisé
examples.suggested: montre comment utiliser ce modèle
examples.why: 'démontrer' means to prove. For a tutorial, 'montrer' is the natural word, and the active infinitive reads less stiffly.

editor_note: Entry 27 is accurate and reads naturally: the trade-off keeps its direction ("réduire `rep_delay` diminue le temps total d'exécution sur le QPU, mais au détriment d'un taux d'erreur de préparation d'état plus élevé"), the 250 microseconds default and "most backends" qualifier are kept, and it uses informal "tu" (consulte).

The three rewritten entries match the English with no drift: "Documentation API `environment`/`execution`", "réinitialiser les qubits à l'état fondamental pour chaque shot", and "Consulte la documentation API [ExecutionOptionsV2]" in the informal "tu" register.

Entries 25 and 26 are faithful and read naturally: "fenêtre d'utilisation glissante de 28 jours", the limited-instance rule (pending workloads "resteront dans la file d'attente", while active ones, "y compris les charges de travail en mode session", keep running) and the not-limited case ("sont susceptibles de s'exécuter avec une priorité plus basse") all keep the English conditions, hedges and caveats.

Entry 22 is faithful and natural: the caveat stays hedged ("Dans certains cas… peuvent atteindre une qualité de solution finale similaire après un post-traitement équivalent"), and the conclusion keeps its recommendation strength ("L'évaluation devrait donc prendre en compte l'ensemble du flux de travail d'optimisation"). It also matches "post-traitement" and "flux de travail" used elsewhere on the page.

The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The benchmark claims in [21] and [32], the Disclaimer caveat in [18] and the binary-to-spin example in [51] all match the source. Terms are consistent (hamiltonien de coût, portes à deux qubits, profondeur de circuit, recherche gloutonne, backend/job/shots), and the text uses tu throughout. A native editor would still smooth three things: the doubled word in "des plans Premium Plan, Flex Plan" in [4], the clumsy "conduit tous deux" in [21], and the stiff "La fonction optimiseur" in [12].

examples.source: available only to IBM Quantum® Premium Plan, Flex Plan, and On-Prem ... Plan users
examples.translation: pour les utilisateurs des plans Premium Plan, Flex Plan et On-Prem (via l'API IBM Quantum Platform) d'IBM Quantum®
examples.suggested: pour les utilisateurs des offres Premium, Flex et On-Prem (via l'API IBM Quantum Platform) d'IBM Quantum®
examples.why: 'plans Premium Plan' says 'plan' twice, which is a calque a native editor would remove.

examples.source: Post-processing of both the random and optimizer results leads to exact ground states
examples.translation: Le post-traitement des résultats aléatoires et de l'optimiseur conduit tous deux à des états fondamentaux exacts
examples.suggested: Après post-traitement, les résultats aléatoires comme ceux de l'optimiseur aboutissent à des états fondamentaux exacts
examples.why: 'tous deux' has no plural subject to refer to, so the sentence is awkward, though the meaning is intact.

examples.source: The optimizer function routes the problem definition to the Parity Twine Compiler.
examples.translation: La fonction optimiseur achemine la définition du problème vers le Parity Twine Compiler.
examples.suggested: La fonction d'optimisation transmet la définition du problème au Parity Twine Compiler.
examples.why: 'fonction optimiseur' copies the English noun-noun structure, and 'achemine' is stiff in this context.

editor_note: Entries 64 and 65 are faithful and idiomatic: "Consulte l'API de l'[Estimator `qiskit-ibm-runtime`]" and "Consulte l'API du [Sampler `qiskit-ibm-runtime`]" use the same informal "Consulte l'API des…" pattern as entries 61-62 and keep Estimator/Sampler in English, as the rest of the page does.

The French keeps the meaning of the English throughout, including the deprecation timelines in [3] ("sera supprimé début 2025", "dans Qiskit SDK v2.0.0"), and uses "tu" correctly ("Tu peux maintenant accomplir cela"). Terms are consistent: "portes fractionnaires", "contrôle au niveau des impulsions", "plannings d'impulsions".

All nine rewritten entries match their English: the twirling precedence rule in [21] ("le produit de `num_randomizations` et de `shots_per_randomization` … est utilisé") keeps its meaning, the "Documentation API `…`" links are consistent, and [105] uses the informal "tu" throughout ("Consulte", "Décide du mode d'exécution … ton job").

Entry 6 is faithful and natural. "Qiskit Serverless bénéficie d'une mise à niveau, et ses fonctionnalités évoluent rapidement" keeps the ongoing-change caveat. "retrouve les notes de version et la documentation la plus récente" keeps the informal tu register and the English meaning.

Entry [35] translates "quantum-centric supercomputing" as "calcul superclassique centré sur le quantique". That drops the supercomputing (HPC) concept and adds a nonexistent "superclassical" computing paradigm, so a learner gets a false idea of IBM's quantum-centric supercomputing. It should be "supercalcul centré sur le quantique". Everything else is faithful. There are minor calques: in [18], "suivis par rapport au job parent" copies "tracked against", and "rattachés au job parent" reads better. In [28], "avoir authentifié Qiskit Serverless" reverses who authenticates, and it should be "t'être authentifié auprès de Qiskit Serverless". In [27], "il ne peut pas avoir de sous-répertoires" is stiff.

examples.source: Qiskit Serverless and quantum-centric supercomputing
examples.translation: Qiskit Serverless et le calcul superclassique centré sur le quantique
examples.suggested: Qiskit Serverless et le supercalcul centré sur le quantique
examples.why: 'Superclassique' is made up and misstates the concept. The source means supercomputing (HPC) combined with quantum, not a 'superclassical' kind of computing.

examples.source: Be sure you have authenticated to Qiskit Serverless with your IBM Quantum account
examples.translation: Assure-toi d'avoir authentifié Qiskit Serverless avec ton compte IBM Quantum
examples.suggested: Assure-toi de t'être authentifié auprès de Qiskit Serverless avec ton compte IBM Quantum
examples.why: The French makes Qiskit Serverless the thing being authenticated. In the source, the user authenticates to the service.

examples.source: are tracked against the parent Qiskit Serverless job
examples.translation: soient suivis par rapport au job Qiskit Serverless parent
examples.suggested: soient rattachés au job Qiskit Serverless parent
examples.why: 'Suivis par rapport à' copies the English 'tracked against' and reads stiffly in French.

examples.source: and cannot have `/data/folder/` subdirectories
examples.translation: et il ne peut pas avoir de sous-répertoires `/data/folder/`
examples.suggested: et ne peut pas contenir de sous-répertoires `/data/folder/`
examples.why: 'Avoir' is a literal rendering of 'have'. French uses 'contenir' for a directory holding subdirectories.

editor_note: Entry 14 is faithful and idiomatic: "Répartir la tâche entre les workers" keeps the meaning of "Distribute task across workers", and it keeps "workers" in English, as French developers usually do, which also matches the @distribute_task code that follows.

The meaning is faithful and would not mislead a learner. It uses informal "tu" throughout and translates the no-cloning theorem (théorème de non-clonage) and projective measurements (mesures projectives) correctly. In [5], "inner products" is rendered as the calque "produits intérieurs". A French quantum-information text would say "produits scalaires", and "produit intérieur" in French usually means the interior product of differential geometry. Also in [5], "limitations fondamentales sur l'information quantique" is a slight calque of English "limitations on"; "de l'information quantique" reads more naturally.

examples.source: including *inner products* between vectors
examples.translation: notamment les *produits intérieurs* entre vecteurs
examples.suggested: notamment les *produits scalaires* entre vecteurs
examples.why: 'Produit scalaire' is the standard French term for the inner product of vectors in quantum information. 'Produit intérieur' is a calque that French readers tend to associate with the interior product of differential forms.

examples.source: we'll derive fundamental limitations on quantum information
examples.translation: nous déduirons des limitations fondamentales sur l'information quantique
examples.suggested: nous établirons des limitations fondamentales de l'information quantique
examples.why: 'limitations ... sur' copies the English preposition; 'limitations de' (or 'limites fondamentales de') is the natural French construction.

editor_note: The course concept "single systems" is narrowed in [2] to "systèmes à un seul qubit", although the lesson deals with single systems in general (arbitrary classical state sets, not only qubits). [5] renders the same concept correctly as "système unique", so the page is inconsistent. [3] also adds a "one" that is not in the source: "qubit systems" becomes "systèmes à un qubit". A learner could briefly misjudge the lesson's scope, but [4] and [5] frame it correctly, so this is not misleading overall. There is also a small calque in [4], "extraire de l'information classique depuis des états quantiques", where "extraire ... de" is more idiomatic.

examples.source: steps you through the content in this lesson on single systems
examples.translation: te guide à travers le contenu de cette leçon sur les systèmes à un seul qubit
examples.suggested: te guide à travers le contenu de cette leçon sur les systèmes uniques
examples.why: The lesson covers single systems with arbitrary classical state sets, not only one qubit. The French narrows the scope and does not match 'système unique' in [5].

examples.source: unitary matrices for operations on qubit systems
examples.translation: les matrices unitaires pour les opérations sur les systèmes à un qubit
examples.suggested: les matrices unitaires pour les opérations sur les systèmes de qubits
examples.why: The translation adds a 'one' ('à un qubit') that is not in the source.

examples.source: measurements that allow classical information to be extracted from quantum states
examples.translation: les mesures permettant d'extraire de l'information classique depuis des états quantiques
examples.suggested: les mesures permettant d'extraire de l'information classique des états quantiques
examples.why: 'Extraire ... depuis' is a calque of 'extracted from'. In French, 'extraire' normally takes 'de'.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: the facts (20 questions, pass mark of 16, lock after two failed attempts) and the Credly notice all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few things. [8] "tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16" is ungrammatical, because répondre takes "à", so the "en" doesn't fit. "note de passage" in [8] and [9] is a Canadian calque, and "badging exam" becomes "examen de certification" in [7], which suggests a formal certification rather than a badge. The course title is left in English in [5] ("Foundations of quantum error correction") but translated in [7], and "Félicitations pour avoir terminé" should be "Félicitations d'avoir terminé".

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass. Upon receiving a passing score
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16 pour le réussir. Dès que tu obtiens une note de passage
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour le réussir. Dès que tu obtiens la note requise
examples.why: 'en répondre ... à' is ungrammatical, and 'note de passage' is a Canadian calque that is uncommon in France.

examples.source: where you can take the badging exam for Foundations of quantum error correction
examples.translation: où tu pourras passer l'examen de certification pour les Fondements de la correction d'erreurs quantiques
examples.suggested: où tu pourras passer l'examen donnant droit au badge du cours Fondements de la correction d'erreurs quantiques
examples.why: A digital badge is not a certification, so 'certification' overstates it slightly. The title is also translated here but left in English in [5].

examples.source: Congratulations on completing the "Foundations of quantum error correction" course by IBM!
examples.translation: Félicitations pour avoir terminé le cours "Foundations of quantum error correction" d'IBM !
examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé le cours « Fondements de la correction d'erreurs quantiques » d'IBM !
examples.why: 'Félicitations pour avoir' is a calque. French uses 'Félicitations d'avoir' and « » quotation marks, and the title should match [1] and [7].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Asymptotic optimality, the lower bound that was already known, the quadratic boost from amplitude amplification and the caveat about practical advantage are all kept, and the terms are correct ("borne inférieure", "amplification d'amplitude", "accélération en racine carrée"). The problems are naturalness only. The heading "Remarques conclusives" is unidiomatic ("Remarques finales" or "Conclusion" is the usual form). Entry [6] hedges twice with "ne soit peut-être pas susceptible de", which the English does not do. Entry [2] ends on the calque "C'est quelque chose qui a été démontré".

examples.source: Concluding remarks
examples.translation: Remarques conclusives
examples.suggested: Remarques finales
examples.why: 'Remarques conclusives' is rare and sounds stiff. A French course would use 'Remarques finales' or 'Conclusion'.

examples.source: although Grover's algorithm may not lead to a practical quantum advantage for searching any time soon
examples.translation: bien que l'algorithme de Grover ne soit peut-être pas susceptible de conduire à un avantage quantique pratique
examples.suggested: bien que l'algorithme de Grover ne mène sans doute pas de sitôt à un avantage quantique pratique pour la recherche
examples.why: The English hedges once ('may not'). Stacking 'peut-être' and 'susceptible de' reads as heavy translationese.

examples.source: This is something that has been proved rigorously in multiple ways.
examples.translation: C'est quelque chose qui a été démontré rigoureusement de plusieurs façons.
examples.suggested: Ce résultat a été démontré rigoureusement de plusieurs façons.
examples.why: 'C'est quelque chose qui' copies the English sentence structure. A native technical writer would name the result directly.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. It uses the standard French terms throughout, such as "mesures projectives", "mesures dans la base standard", "discrimination d'états quantiques", "tomographie d'état quantique" and "description en matrice densité", and it uses the informal "tu" correctly ("te guide", "Télécharge les diapositives").

The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The "tu" register is consistent (te guide, Télécharge), and the core terms (matrice densité, fidélité, dilatation, théorème d'Uhlmann) are correct. The problem is entry [3]: "traced out" is calqued as "est tracé", when a French writer would say "on prend la trace partielle sur…". The phrase "qui nous laisse avec ρ" is also an anglicism, and "fondamentalement important" reads stiffly.

examples.line_approx: Une purification d'un état quantique ... lorsque le reste du système composé est tracé.
examples.source: a pure state of a larger compound system that leaves us with ρ when the rest of the compound system is traced out
examples.translation: un état pur d'un système composé plus grand qui nous laisse avec ρ lorsque le reste du système composé est tracé
examples.suggested: un état pur d'un système composé plus grand dont on retrouve ρ en prenant la trace partielle sur le reste du système composé
examples.why: 'être tracé' is a calque of 'traced out'. The conventional French expression is 'prendre la trace partielle (sur)'. 'nous laisse avec' is also an anglicism.

examples.line_approx: à condition que la partie du système composé qui est tracée soit suffisamment grande
examples.source: provided that the portion of the compound system that gets traced out is large enough
examples.translation: à condition que la partie du système composé qui est tracée soit suffisamment grande
examples.suggested: à condition que la partie du système composé sur laquelle on prend la trace partielle soit suffisamment grande
examples.why: Same calque, 'tracée'. Changing it keeps entry [3] consistent with the fix above.

examples.line_approx: Cette leçon est centrée sur un concept fondamentalement important
examples.source: centered around a fundamentally important concept
examples.translation: centrée sur un concept fondamentalement important
examples.suggested: Cette leçon porte sur un concept fondamental de la théorie de l'information quantique
examples.why: 'fondamentalement important' is a word-for-word rendering and reads stiffly in French.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the badge conditions, the HPC/quantum audience split and the Credly privacy notice, and the "tu" register holds. A native editor would still fix a few calques. In [11], "Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu les leçons" has a dangling infinitive: grammatically, it is the exam that has read the lessons. In [16], "réclamer ton badge" is a calque of "claim" where the usual word is "récupérer", and "Afin de t'émettre un IBM Digital Badge" is stiff. The gender-inclusive "celles et ceux" and "notifié·e" also sit beside the plain masculine "Les apprenants" and "Les employés", which is an inconsistency.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu les leçons de ce cours.
examples.suggested: Cet examen est à passer une fois que tu as lu les leçons de ce cours.
examples.why: Dangling infinitive: the implied subject of 'avoir lu' is 'cet examen'. The sentence is calqued on the English passive.

examples.source: You will receive an email notification from Credly with instructions for claiming the badge.
examples.translation: Tu recevras une notification par e-mail de la part de Credly avec les instructions pour réclamer ton badge.
examples.suggested: Tu recevras de Credly un e-mail t'expliquant comment récupérer ton badge.
examples.why: Here 'réclamer' is a calque of 'claim'. It suggests demanding or complaining, and 'récupérer' is the idiomatic word.

examples.source: Learners can skip over sections in their own area of expertise as appropriate.
examples.translation: Les apprenants peuvent sauter les sections relevant de leur propre domaine d'expertise, selon ce qui leur convient.
examples.suggested: Tu peux sauter les sections qui relèvent de ton domaine d'expertise.
examples.why: The same entry uses the inclusive 'celles et ceux' and then the masculine 'Les apprenants'. The line could also address the reader directly, which matches the tu register.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (5, 8, 9, 12) would mislead a learner. The 20 questions, the 16 correct answers needed to pass, the two attempts before a temporary lock and the list of data shared with Credly all match the English, and the "tu" register holds throughout. Entry 8 uses "note de passage", which is Quebec usage and stiff in France French. Entry 9 says the same thing as "note minimale requise", so the two adjacent entries don't match. Entry 12 has stiff wording in "Afin de t'émettre un IBM Digital Badge" (délivrer is the usual verb) and in "à des fins de rapports et d'opérations du programme".

examples.source: Upon receiving a passing score, your badge will automatically be sent
examples.translation: Après avoir obtenu une note de passage, ton badge sera automatiquement envoyé
examples.suggested: Une fois l'examen réussi, ton badge sera automatiquement envoyé
examples.why: "note de passage" is Quebec usage and reads oddly in France French. Entry 9 uses "note minimale requise" for the same idea, so the two entries should match.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge
examples.translation: Afin de t'émettre un IBM Digital Badge
examples.suggested: Afin de te délivrer un IBM Digital Badge
examples.why: "émettre" copies the English "issue". French normally uses "délivrer" for a badge or certificate.

examples.source: for program reporting and operational purposes
examples.translation: à des fins de rapports et d'opérations du programme
examples.suggested: à des fins de suivi et de gestion opérationnelle du programme
examples.why: "fins de rapports et d'opérations" copies the English word for word. Legal French would put it more idiomatically.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and the tu register is kept. A few calques would read as English to a French editor. "scaling" of the approaches is rendered "mise à l'échelle" in [4], which is the infrastructure sense; for algorithmic cost it should be "passage à l'échelle". In [16] "data processor" is rendered "processeur de données tiers", where GDPR-style French says "sous-traitant". [11] uses a stiff dangling construction ("destiné à être passé après avoir lu", "tu seras notifié par Credly"), and [7]/[16] have the calques "compléter les prérequis" and "réclamer le badge".

examples.source: what factors determine the scaling of approaches
examples.translation: les facteurs qui déterminent la mise à l'échelle des approches
examples.suggested: les facteurs qui déterminent le passage à l'échelle des approches
examples.why: 'Mise à l'échelle' suggests resizing or scaling up infrastructure. For how an algorithm's cost grows, the usual French is 'passage à l'échelle' (or 'comportement en fonction de la taille').

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un processeur de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.suggested: un sous-traitant tiers (au sens du traitement des données) autorisé par IBM
examples.why: Literal calque. The established French legal term for 'data processor' is 'sous-traitant'.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course. After you pass the exam, you will be notified by Credly that you have earned a badge.
examples.translation: Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu les leçons de ce cours. Après avoir réussi l'examen, tu seras notifié par Credly que tu as obtenu un badge.
examples.suggested: Passe cet examen après avoir lu les leçons de ce cours. Une fois l'examen réussi, Credly t'informera que tu as obtenu un badge.
examples.why: The dangling infinitive has the wrong implied subject, and the passive 'être notifié par' is an English calque.

examples.source: We recommend that learners complete the following prerequisites
examples.translation: Nous recommandons aux apprenants de compléter les prérequis suivants
examples.suggested: Nous recommandons aux apprenants de suivre les prérequis suivants
examples.why: 'Compléter' in the sense of 'finish' is an anglicism. 'Suivre' or 'acquérir' is idiomatic.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (8, 39, 84) say what the English says. The dataset definition, the i-indexed basis-state ordering with |i⟩ given by the binary representation of i, the normalization constant α, and the R_Y(2θ) remark with rescaling to (0,2π] are all correct, and none of them would mislead a learner. There is one naturalness slip in entry 8. The closing sentence copies the English "refer to ... as" twice ("nous nous référerons principalement au chargement…", "nous nous référerons … à un seul vecteur … comme $\vec{x}$"). A French technical writer would write "nous traiterons surtout du chargement…" and "nous désignerons simplement par $\vec{x}$…".

examples.source: But we will mostly refer to the loading of a single vector from our dataset at a time, and will often simply refer to a single vector of $N$ features as $\vec{x}$.
examples.translation: Mais nous nous référerons principalement au chargement d'un seul vecteur de notre jeu de données à la fois, et nous nous référerons souvent simplement à un seul vecteur de $N$ caractéristiques comme $\vec{x}$.
examples.suggested: Mais nous traiterons surtout du chargement d'un seul vecteur du jeu de données à la fois, et nous désignerons souvent simplement un tel vecteur de $N$ caractéristiques par $\vec{x}$.
examples.why: « se référer à X comme Y » is an anglicism, and it is used twice here. The meaning is intact, but a native editor would change it.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries are faithful. They use "tu" consistently. Entry 29 keeps both comparisons ("plus fort que le hasard indépendant et plus fort que ce que peut expliquer une corrélation purement classique ou un hasard partagé"). Entry 52 renders queue time, limited availability and device constraints as "temps d'attente en file, une disponibilité limitée, et des contraintes spécifiques au dispositif", which matches "dispositif" used elsewhere on the page.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The scope of lessons 2-6, 7-8, 10-14, the QPU-time caveat and the deprecated-snippet warning all match the source, and "tu" is used consistently. A native editor would still fix a few calques. "labs"/"computational lab activity" becomes "laboratoires"/"activité de laboratoire informatique", where French teaching material says "TP"/"travaux pratiques". "Good-faith estimates" becomes "estimations de bonne foi", which is a literal calque. Entry [3] also adds "approfondie", which is not in the source.

examples.source: Each lesson consists of a PDF that was used in a lecture context, and a computational lab activity. In some cases, the labs are sparse...
examples.translation: ainsi qu'une activité de laboratoire informatique. Dans certains cas, les laboratoires sont succincts...
examples.suggested: ainsi que des travaux pratiques sur ordinateur. Dans certains cas, les TP sont succincts...
examples.why: 'Laboratoire' for a coding exercise is an anglicism. French course material calls these travaux pratiques (TP).

examples.source: Good-faith estimates of required QPU time have been provided at the top of each lesson
examples.translation: Des estimations de bonne foi du temps QPU requis ont été fournies en tête de chaque leçon
examples.suggested: Une estimation indicative du temps QPU nécessaire figure en tête de chaque leçon
examples.why: 'De bonne foi' is a literal calque that sounds legalistic in French. 'Indicative' carries the intended hedge.

examples.source: the labs contain detailed explanations and mathematical motivation.
examples.translation: des explications détaillées et une motivation mathématique approfondie.
examples.suggested: des explications détaillées et la motivation mathématique sous-jacente.
examples.why: 'Approfondie' is not in the source and slightly overstates it. This is a minor addition that does not mislead.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout, "algorithmes variationnels" and "primitives IBM Quantum" are correct, and the page uses "tu" consistently. Two English calques remain. In [11], "réclamer ton badge" copies "claim the badge"; in French "réclamer" suggests making a demand, so "récupérer" or "accepter ton badge" reads more naturally. In [6], the passive "tu seras notifié par Credly" is stiff; "Credly t'informera" or "tu recevras une notification de Credly" is more idiomatic.

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: This copies "claim". In French, "réclamer" suggests making a demand, while "récupérer" or "accepter" is the usual wording for a digital badge.

examples.source: you will be notified by Credly that you have earned a badge
examples.translation: tu seras notifié par Credly que tu as obtenu un badge
examples.suggested: Credly t'informera que tu as obtenu un badge
examples.why: This keeps the English passive structure, which is stiff in French; the active voice is more natural.

editor_note: Both rewritten link labels are accurate and use the same terms as the rest of the page: entry 54 gives "Découplage dynamique" and entry 55 gives "Résilience, incluant l'atténuation des erreurs de mesure et l'extrapolation à bruit nul (ZNE)". "y compris" would be a slightly more idiomatic alternative to "incluant", but the current wording is fine.

The translation is faithful throughout. The SABRE/AI/Rustiq comparisons, the caveats about mirror circuits and the recommendations all keep their meaning, and the core terms (transpileur IA, gestionnaires de passes, profondeur à deux qubits, circuit miroir) are consistent. There are still a few slips a native editor would fix. [71] opens with "Construit", which is the third-person form, not the tu imperative "Construis", and then switches to noun phrases. [60] renders "tracking closely on most circuits" as "se rapprochant étroitement de la plupart des circuits", which is awkward and loses the sense of tracking the other methods. Smaller calques appear in [63] ("reçoivent du crédit"), [59] ("s'explique … parce que") and [97] ("la valeur par défaut recommandée" for a method).

examples.source: Build the mirror circuits (append $U^\dagger$), remap to contiguous qubit indices ..., and run on a noisy Aer simulator.
examples.translation: Construit les circuits miroirs (ajout de $U^\dagger$), remappage vers des indices de qubits contigus ..., et exécution sur un simulateur Aer bruité.
examples.suggested: Construis les circuits miroirs (ajoute $U^\dagger$), remappe-les vers des indices de qubits contigus ..., puis exécute-les sur un simulateur Aer bruité.
examples.why: 'Construit' is the wrong verb form for tu. The sentence also switches from a verb to noun phrases partway through.

examples.source: tracking closely on most circuits without many outliers
examples.translation: se rapprochant étroitement de la plupart des circuits sans beaucoup de valeurs aberrantes
examples.suggested: restant très proche des autres méthodes sur la plupart des circuits, avec peu de valeurs aberrantes
examples.why: It is a calque that reads as though the transpiler gets close to the circuits, which blurs the intended meaning: its results stay close to those of the other methods.

examples.source: When a tie occurs, all tied methods receive credit
examples.translation: toutes les méthodes à égalité reçoivent du crédit
examples.suggested: toutes les méthodes à égalité sont comptabilisées
examples.why: 'Recevoir du crédit' is a calque of the English; 'être comptabilisé' is the idiomatic French.

examples.source: **SABRE** is the recommended default.
examples.translation: **SABRE** est la valeur par défaut recommandée.
examples.suggested: **SABRE** est le choix par défaut recommandé.
examples.why: SABRE is a method, not a value, so 'valeur' is the wrong word here.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix a few things. In [12], "quantum-centric supercomputing" becomes the awkward "architecture d'informatique supercalculée quantique-centrique". In [11], "un comportement différent que le modéliser dans l'eau" is ungrammatical. In [31], "retélécharger" for "re-upload" reads as re-downloading. In [18], "Veuillez consulter" slips into the formal register in a file that otherwise uses "tu".

examples.source: We showcase a quantum-centric supercomputing architecture in miniature
examples.translation: Nous présentons une architecture d'informatique supercalculée quantique-centrique en miniature
examples.suggested: Nous présentons, en miniature, une architecture de supercalcul centrée sur le quantique
examples.why: 'informatique supercalculée' is not a French term, and 'quantique-centrique' is a calque.

examples.source: Modeling a compound in the air (in vacuo) will describe different behavior than modeling it in water.
examples.translation: Modéliser un composé dans l'air (in vacuo) décrira un comportement différent que le modéliser dans l'eau.
examples.suggested: Modéliser un composé dans l'air (in vacuo) ne donnera pas le même comportement que le modéliser dans l'eau.
examples.why: 'différent que' followed by an infinitive is ungrammatical. It should be 'différent de' plus a noun phrase, or the sentence needs recasting.

examples.source: re-upload it any time we change its source code
examples.translation: le retélécharger chaque fois que nous modifions son code source
examples.suggested: le téléverser à nouveau chaque fois que nous modifions son code source
examples.why: 'télécharger' usually means download, so 'retélécharger' reverses the direction of the transfer for many readers. 'téléverser' is unambiguous.

examples.source: Please refer to the SQD IEF-PCM Qiskit Function template
examples.translation: Veuillez consulter le [modèle de fonction Qiskit SQD IEF-PCM]
examples.suggested: Consulte le [modèle de fonction Qiskit SQD IEF-PCM]
examples.why: Formal 'veuillez' breaks the informal 'tu' convention used everywhere else in the file.

editor_note: The seven rewritten titles are faithful and consistent with the rest of the page: "répartition de marché" in entries 69/70 matches entry 67, and "Annulation probabiliste des erreurs" in entry 88 matches entry 84. "Ensemble indépendant maximum" in entry 68 correctly keeps maximum rather than maximal.

Entries 6, 87 and 99 match their English. They keep "feedforward classique", "mesures en milieu de circuit (MCM)" and "profondeur à deux qubits" consistent with the rest of the page, and the key claims survive: constant depth for dynamic circuits, linear SWAP-chain growth for the unitary version, and parallel measurements that still carry a fixed cost. Only entry 103 needs changes, and neither misleads. The link title uses the anglicism "Benchmarker", which a native editor would replace with "Évaluer les performances des…". The lead-in "tu pourrais être intéressé(e) par" is a calque with an awkward gender marker; "ces ressources pourraient t'intéresser" reads more naturally.

examples.source: Benchmark dynamic circuits with cut Bell pairs
examples.translation: Benchmarker les circuits dynamiques avec des paires de Bell coupées
examples.suggested: Évaluer les performances des circuits dynamiques avec des paires de Bell coupées
examples.why: "Benchmarker" is an anglicized verb. French technical writing prefers "évaluer les performances" or "étalonner", especially in a title.

examples.source: If you found this work interesting, you might be interested in the following materials:
examples.translation: Si tu as trouvé ce travail intéressant, tu pourrais être intéressé(e) par les ressources suivantes :
examples.suggested: Si ce travail t'a intéressé, les ressources suivantes pourraient aussi te plaire :
examples.why: This copies the English sentence structure, and the "intéressé(e)" gender marker is clumsy. Turning the sentence around avoids both and reads like native writing.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (23, 25, 37, 41, 44) would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful: k_max being "bien inférieur au k unique", the MPF combining "nombres classiques, pas des états quantiques", and the state-preparation caveat all carry over intact, and expectation value→valeur moyenne is used consistently. The informal "tu" is used correctly in 37 and 41. Entry 44 has two small naturalness slips. It renders "two stages" as "deux étapes", which clashes with the page's numbered "Étape 1–4" sections. It also uses the calque "exemple de simulateur à petite échelle" instead of "exemple à petite échelle sur simulateur", which would match the following "exemple à grande échelle sur du matériel".

examples.source: walks through an end-to-end MPF workflow in two stages
examples.translation: parcourt un flux de travail MPF de bout en bout en deux étapes
examples.suggested: présente un flux de travail MPF complet, de bout en bout, en deux temps
examples.why: The page's workflow sections are titled "Étape 1–4" (see the link to [Étape 4] in entry 25), so "deux étapes" reads as if it refers to those numbered steps.

examples.source: a **small-scale simulator example** (10-qubit Heisenberg chain)
examples.translation: un **exemple de simulateur à petite échelle**
examples.suggested: un **exemple à petite échelle sur simulateur**
examples.why: This is a calque of the English noun stack: "à petite échelle" ends up describing the simulator instead of the example. The suggested wording also matches "exemple à grande échelle sur du matériel" in the next sentence.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and core terms are correct and consistent: hamiltonien, état fondamental, NP-difficile, backend, job, transpilé, "tu" register. A few phrasings still read as translated rather than written in French. [37] "Facultativement, utilise options" is stiff and leaves `options` bare in the sentence. [38] "`transpile_only` choisit si" is a calque. [12] "cette frustration se combine globalement" weakens "compounded", which means amplified. [17] "doit être mise à l'échelle en fonction du" is a clumsy calque of "scale with".

examples.source: Optionally, use options for additional control over the submission:
examples.translation: Facultativement, utilise options pour un contrôle supplémentaire sur la soumission :
examples.suggested: Tu peux aussi utiliser `options` pour mieux contrôler la soumission :
examples.why: "Facultativement" at the start of the sentence is stiff, and the bare word "options" reads like a grammar mistake in French.

examples.source: `transpile_only` chooses if the problem is only transpiled to a circuit (and not solved)
examples.translation: `transpile_only` choisit si le problème est uniquement transpilé en circuit (et non résolu)
examples.suggested: `transpile_only` indique si le problème est seulement transpilé en circuit (sans être résolu)
examples.why: "Choisit si" is a literal calque. A parameter "indique" or "détermine" something.

examples.source: this frustration is compounded globally
examples.translation: cette frustration se combine globalement
examples.suggested: cette frustration s'amplifie à l'échelle du système entier
examples.why: "Compounded" means intensified. "Se combine" weakens this and reads awkwardly.

examples.source: the variance of the couplings must scale with the number of particles
examples.translation: la variance des couplages doit être mise à l'échelle en fonction du nombre de particules
examples.suggested: la variance des couplages doit dépendre du nombre de particules
examples.why: "Mise à l'échelle en fonction de" is a clumsy calque of "scale with". "Dépendre de" or "varier avec" is more natural.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the caveats. Nothing would mislead a learner: the MEM-only-on-the-orbit-curve warning [43], the point that MEM cannot rewrite a mid-circuit result already used in feedforward [50], and the note that this is not a reproduction of Figure 2a [55] all carry over intact. The problems are consistency and phrasing. The same thing gets two names: "job" is "tâche" in [4]/[5] but "job" from [12] on, and the batch is "lot" in [5] but "batch" elsewhere. The product name "Quantum Compute" is translated as "calcul quantique" in reference [60], though it stays in English in [5]. There are also calques such as "20 entrées échantillonnées fois les trois stratégies" [47] and "Résultats d'apprentissage" [6].

examples.source: partitioning circuit sizes across three Quantum Compute jobs in one batch
examples.translation: sur trois tâches Quantum Compute dans un même lot
examples.suggested: sur trois jobs Quantum Compute dans un même batch
examples.why: From [12] on, the file uses 'job'/'batch' everywhere, so the early 'tâche'/'lot' here (and 'tâches' in [4]) splits one concept across two names.

examples.source: Quantum Compute limitations for stretch variables
examples.translation: Limitations de calcul quantique pour les variables d'étirement
examples.suggested: Limitations de Quantum Compute pour les variables stretch
examples.why: 'Quantum Compute' is an IBM service name, left untranslated in [5]; turning it into 'calcul quantique' makes it read like a general concept.

examples.source: 20 sampled inputs times the three strategies
examples.translation: 20 entrées échantillonnées fois les trois stratégies
examples.suggested: 20 entrées échantillonnées multipliées par les trois stratégies
examples.why: 'fois' used as a multiplication connector in running prose is an English calque.

examples.source: Learning outcomes
examples.translation: Résultats d'apprentissage
examples.suggested: Objectifs d'apprentissage
examples.why: 'Objectifs d'apprentissage' is the conventional heading in French teaching material.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The quantities are preserved: O(N^2) entries, N(N+1)/2 unique entries, row 15 / column 20, x1=14 / x2=19. The simulator and hardware caveats are intact, and the "tu" register is kept consistently. The problems are calques. "inner product" becomes "produit interne" where French uses "produit scalaire". "cosets" is kept as English "cosets"/"cosets gauches" instead of "classes (à gauche)". "effectively replacing" becomes "remplaçant efficacement", which reads as "efficiently" rather than "in effect". The pattern step "map" becomes "cartographier" (geographic mapping) in the list and the Step 1 heading, and "rendre les catégories de données séparées par un hyperplan" is stiff.

examples.source: effectively replacing classical analogs
examples.translation: remplaçant efficacement les analogues classiques
examples.suggested: remplaçant de fait leurs analogues classiques
examples.why: 'effectively' means 'in effect' here. 'efficacement' suggests efficiency or success, a slight shift in nuance.

examples.source: returns their inner product
examples.translation: renvoie leur produit interne
examples.suggested: renvoie leur produit scalaire
examples.why: The conventional French term is 'produit scalaire'. 'produit interne' is an anglicism (also in the same sentence group at line 88).

examples.source: two cosets formed by a group and subgroup ... two left-cosets
examples.translation: deux cosets formés par un groupe ... deux cosets gauches
examples.suggested: deux classes formées par un groupe et un sous-groupe ... deux classes à gauche
examples.why: French group theory says 'classe (à gauche)', not 'coset'. 'cosets gauches' is a hybrid calque.

examples.source: map, optimize, execute, and post-process
examples.translation: cartographier, optimiser, exécuter et post-traiter
examples.suggested: transposer (ou mapper), optimiser, exécuter et post-traiter
examples.why: 'cartographier' means drawing a map. Here the step means mapping classical inputs onto a quantum problem. The same issue is in the Step 1 heading (entry 25).

examples.source: The goal of Psi(x) is to make categories of data separated by a hyperplane.
examples.translation: L'objectif de Psi(x) est de rendre les catégories de données séparées par un hyperplan.
examples.suggested: L'objectif de Psi(x) est de rendre les catégories de données séparables par un hyperplan.
examples.why: 'rendre ... séparées' is stiff calqued syntax. 'séparables' is the natural ML phrasing.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 10 keeps the English meaning. The next-generation batteries, the Li-S bond breaking, the molecular-level scope and the "more broadly" hedge about reaction pathways and catalysts are all there, with no drift or invented claims. The second sentence still reads like translated English. "fournit un aperçu au niveau moléculaire pertinent pour comprendre" copies "provides insight" word for word, and "aperçu" means a glimpse or overview, not an insight. "Calculer comment l'énergie évolue" is stiff, and the doubled "pour ... pour" in the last sentence reads awkwardly.

examples.source: Calculating how energy changes as a Li–S bond breaks provides molecular-level insight relevant to understanding the chemical transformations in these systems.
examples.translation: Calculer comment l'énergie évolue lorsqu'une liaison Li-S se rompt fournit un aperçu au niveau moléculaire pertinent pour comprendre les transformations chimiques dans ces systèmes.
examples.suggested: Calculer l'évolution de l'énergie lors de la rupture d'une liaison Li-S apporte un éclairage à l'échelle moléculaire utile pour comprendre les transformations chimiques de ces systèmes.
examples.why: "Fournit un aperçu" copies "provides insight", and "aperçu" means a glimpse or overview, not an insight. "Calculer comment" is stiff. The meaning is still correct.

examples.source: potential energy surfaces are tools for studying reaction pathways and catalysts for more resource-efficient chemical processes.
examples.translation: les surfaces d'énergie potentielle sont des outils pour étudier les voies réactionnelles et les catalyseurs pour des processus chimiques plus économes en ressources.
examples.suggested: les surfaces d'énergie potentielle permettent d'étudier les voies réactionnelles et les catalyseurs au service de procédés chimiques plus économes en ressources.
examples.why: The doubled "pour ... pour" copies the English structure and reads awkwardly. The meaning is faithful.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveats in [75] (does not reach chemical accuracy, changes "pourrait améliorer" but need further testing) and [76] (interactions removed, adjusted circuit) are kept intact, and the text uses "tu" consistently. The problems are small editorial ones. "Middleware" is rendered as "intergiciel" in [6] but as "bibliothèque middleware" in [21]. In [75], "le résultat se termine à environ 23.7 kcal/mol au-dessus" is a calque of "finishes … above". Decimals keep the English point (1.0 Å, 23.7 kcal/mol) where French uses a comma. The "Requirements" heading [35] is translated as "Prérequis", the same word as the "Prerequisites" heading [11], so the page ends up with two identical section titles.

examples.source: the result finishes approximately 23.7 kcal/mol above the reference energy
examples.translation: le résultat se termine à environ 23.7 kcal/mol au-dessus de l'énergie de référence
examples.suggested: le résultat se situe à environ 23,7 kcal/mol au-dessus de l'énergie de référence
examples.why: "Se termine à" is a literal calque of "finishes". French technical writing says "se situe à" or "s'établit à" and uses a decimal comma.

examples.source: a middleware library written in Rust
examples.translation: une bibliothèque middleware écrite en Rust
examples.suggested: une bibliothèque intergicielle écrite en Rust (or use "middleware" in [6] too)
examples.why: Entry [6] renders middleware as "intergiciel". Pick one term and use it throughout the file.

examples.source: Requirements
examples.translation: Prérequis
examples.suggested: Configuration requise
examples.why: Entry [11] (Prerequisites) is already "Prérequis", so the page now has two identical section headings.

examples.source: at a bond distance of 1.0 $\AA$
examples.translation: à une distance de liaison de 1.0 $\AA$
examples.suggested: à une distance de liaison de 1,0 $\AA$
examples.why: French typography uses a decimal comma. The same fix applies in [34] and [73].

editor_note: The rewritten entry [7] is accurate: the conditional "peut soutenir", the "de plus en plus complexes" systems and the stability-prediction framing all match the English. It has two minor problems. It renders "workflow" as "flux de travail", but the rest of the page, including the title [1] and entries [6], [12] and [23], keeps "workflow", so the term is now inconsistent. "À travers un flux de travail" is also a calque of "through"; a French technical writer would more likely write "au moyen d'un workflow".

examples.source: through a hybrid quantum–classical classification workflow
examples.translation: à travers un flux de travail de classification hybride quantique-classique
examples.suggested: au moyen d'un workflow de classification hybride quantique-classique
examples.why: Every other entry on the page uses "workflow" ([1], [6], [12], [23]), so "flux de travail" is the only place the term changes. "À travers" is also a literal calque of "through".

editor_note: The four rewritten entries are faithful and use informal "tu" throughout ("Ton temps d'exécution peut varier", "consulte [le manuscrit publié]"), and entry 8 sensibly repairs the source's truncated "The Optimization" to "L'Optimization Solver" while keeping "à l'échelle utilitaire" and the product names Optimization Solver and Performance Management consistent with the rest of the page.
